newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Renault to take 96 French job cut charge.
newsitem.headline: Renault to take 96 French job cut charge.

text.p: French carmarker Renault will take a charge in its 1996 results for a plan to cut jobs in France, chairman Louis Schweitzer said on Tuesday.
"When we announce a job reduction plan before we draw up the accounts the logic is to provision it in those accounts," Schweitzer told reporters at the Geneva car show.

He declined to comment on union calculations that the group would show a net six billion franc loss comprising two billion in operating losses, 2.5 billion from the previously announced closure of a Belgium plant and around 1.5 billion for the French job cut proposal.
He said he would not discuss the results until their announcement on March 20.

Renault senior officials have said the group will accelerate its job reduction programme and plans to announce 2,764 job cuts in France to the staff works council on March 13, nearly double the cuts in 1996.

Schweitzer said the Belgian plant closure and the resulting concentration of its European car production would result in savings of 850 million francs. The Belgian plant employs 3,100 people and the company has said it will take a 2.4 billion restructuring charge for the closure.

He said the group was giving no specific figure on savings expected from the job cuts in France as that was part of a progressive improvement in the French operation. He said no outright layoffs were foreseen in France.
Other officials had said the French cuts would rely heavily on early retirement.
Schweitzer has previously said the group aimed to breakeven in 1997. He declined to address this previous forecast, saying he would do so when the results were announced later this month.
